Subject: SCCs module guidance + TIA request

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team is preparing the DPA addendum and has asked us to confirm which SCCs module path Redwood recommends for the transfers that Medilink will have in scope: customer content (PHI-lite), support logs (some identifiers), and aggregate analytics used for product analytics.

We also need a short Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) or outline of residual risk so Legal can include it with the DPA packet when it goes to procurement. Target timeline: get the module decision and TIA summary by end of next week so we can proceed to DocuSign.

Can you confirm:
- Which SCCs module(s) you recommend for the three flows above and why (controller->processor vs processor->processor concerns).
- Whether Redwood will accept Module 2/3 split (if applicable) or needs a single module approach.
- Any evidentiary attachments (TIA summary, subprocessors list, data residency commitments).

Appreciate a short proposed text we can copy into our DPA.

Best,
Elena

Head of Legal Operations
MediLink Health

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: elena.rossi@medilink.com
Date: Thu, 2 Sep 2026 09:43:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SCCs module guidance + TIA request

Laura / Ben — looping you in for quick alignment. Elena asked for a recommended SCCs module path and a short TIA for three distinct flows: customer content (sensitive but not full PHI ingestion), support logs (IDs + timestamps), and aggregate analytics.

My initial read: recommend a hybrid approach and document the rationale explicitly. Proposed recommendation:
- Customer content (primary product traffic): Module 2 (Controller -> Processor) language in the DPA. This keeps obligations explicit for content we process on behalf of customers and maps to our existing controller/processor commitments.
- Support logs (operational telemetry with identifiers): Module 2 as well, but add scoped subprocessors language and additional logging controls in the annex.
- Aggregate analytics (de-identified/aggregated product metrics): Module 3 for processor->processor flows where we share aggregated outputs with partners or analytics vendors.

Rationale: modular split reflects real operational differences and limits over-broad controller->controller obligations where processor-to-processor subsections are more appropriate. We should include a short TIA heatmap that explains residual transfer risk per flow and mitigation measures (encryption-at-rest, access controls, subprocessor commitments, regional routing).

Attachments to prepare for Elena: concise TIA-summary (1 pager), SCCs-module-matrix (table showing mapping per flow), and the exec checklist for Legal/Procurement (DocuSign link + signatures). I attached a draft matrix and a TIA heatmap (see attachments). Can you both review and call out anything missing by EOD Monday? I want to send a consolidated response to Medilink on Tuesday.

Thanks — Jasmine
Jasmine Liu
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, elena.rossi@medilink.com
Date: Fri, 3 Sep 2026 10:17:00 -0700
Subject: RE: SCCs module guidance + TIA request

Jasmine — quick notes after reviewing the draft matrix:

1) Module clarity: I agree with the hybrid split but prefer we frame it as "Primary Module 2 with Module 3 carve-outs for specified analytics outputs." That phrasing tends to be easier to negotiate with customer counsel.

2) TIA items to call out explicitly:
   - Data categories per flow (examples) and expected retention windows (support logs shorter TTL).
   - Subprocessor list + approval mechanism (we should commit to a 30-day notice for new subprocessors for MediLink).
   - Proposed fallback: if UK/EU regulator requires additional safeguards, we will offer SCCs + encryption key residency options under Redwood Private.

3) Evidence/attachments: add SOC 2 report redacted, subprocessors.csv (redacted hostnames), and our most recent DPIA excerpt for the product. Those increase comfort without too much legal friction.

I'll make a brief language suggestion for the DPA paragraph: "Redwood Inference shall apply Module 2 SCCs for transfers of Customer Content and Support Logs, with Module 3 SCCs applying to de-identified, aggregated analytics outputs as set forth in Annex X. Parties acknowledge that the parties' responsibilities and applicable technical and organisational measures are described in the attached TIA summary."

If that sounds good, Ben can confirm commercial timeline and we can push the DocuSign packet.

- Laura
Laura Bennett
VP Legal (Contracts)
Redwood Inference

Elena — thanks for the patience. Below is the consolidated recommendation and the items we're attaching to the DPA package. Please see inline commitments and the DocuSign link at the bottom.

Executive recommendation (to insert verbatim in DPA):
"Redwood Inference recommends applying Module 2 SCCs to transfers of Customer Content and Support Logs processed on behalf of Medilink, with Module 3 SCCs applying to de-identified and aggregate analytics outputs as specified in Annex X. Parties agree that applicable technical and organisational measures for each flow are described in the attached Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) summary."

Summary of attachments (attached to this thread):

- SCCs-module-matrix.pdf — table mapping the three flows to Module 2 / Module 3 and the corresponding contractual clauses.
- SCCs-exec-checklist.xlsx — steps for signature, procurement, and subprocessors follow-up.

- Evidence: redacted SOC 2 and DPIA excerpts can be provided upon NDA (we include redacted versions in the package).
- Fallback: If a regulator requests additional safeguards, Redwood can discuss key residency options under Redwood Private.
